content: Check your blood sugar levels regularly as instructed by your doctor, and share the results with them. If you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination, inform your doctor immediately. Notify your doctor if you have recently undergone surgery, are planning to have surgery, or if you will be immobile for an extended period, such as during a long plane flight. These situations can increase your risk of developing blood clots, particularly if you are using hormonal birth control. This medication may cause blotchy, darkened areas on your face and skin, a condition known as melasma. Sunlight can exacerbate this effect, so limit your exposure to the sun, and avoid tanning booths and sunlamps. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses while on this medication. It may take longer for you to conceive after discontinuing birth control pills. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. If you become pregnant or suspect you might be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. Additionally, this medication may reduce breast milk production, and a small amount of the drug can pass into breast milk, potentially causing undesirable effects in a nursing infant. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some drugs can reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, which may result in pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (such as rifampin and rifabutin), ritonavir, and St. John’s Wort. Inform your doctor when starting any new medication and discuss whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as blood tests for clotting factors or thyroid function, potentially leading to inaccurate results. If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately. In the U.S., contact poison control at 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, regular physical exams, including lab and medical tests such as blood pressure checks, breast exams, pelvic exams, and Pap smears, are recommended. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, the advice may vary depending on the brand and the number of doses missed. Refer to the product package for specific instructions. You may need to use backup birth control methods, such as condoms or spermicides, to prevent pregnancy. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
